name: DGX Spark Ling-3.2-air Atlas (SparkLing 0.1.0)

weights.description: Which checkpoint the engine serves: spark is Primitive AI's NVFP4A16 with NVFP4 prefill and decode and the checkpoint's own MTP drafter; strict is inclusionAI's original dynamic FP8 as published, without drafting.

spark.description: primitive-ai/Ling-3.2-air-NVFP4A16 (MIT, about 78 GB): NVFP4 routed experts with BF16 activations. SparkLing's fast Spark settings: NVFP4 prefill (expert activations for large prompt batches) and NVFP4 decode (attention projections), the published BF16 vocabulary head, and the checkpoint's one-token MTP predictor as the drafter.

strict.description: inclusionAI/Ling-3.2-air (MIT, about 129 GB): the original dynamic block-FP8 checkpoint with its BF16 and FP32 exceptions, checkpoint precision, the published sampling defaults and template, no drafting. Atlas pages cold experts from disk to fit one Spark.

summary: inclusionAI's Ling-3.2-air (124B MoE, 5.5B active) on one DGX Spark with SparkLing 0.1.0's Atlas build: text, image and video input, tools, reasoning, prefix caching and its 262,144-token window. --weights spark (default) serves Primitive AI's NVFP4A16 with NVFP4 prefill and decode and the checkpoint's MTP drafter; --weights strict serves the original FP8. Three modes: default (8 requests), saver (1 request of 8,192 tokens) and max (16 requests). Additive only: no default model, no aliases. Draft: installs once the SparkLing 0.1.0 pins are final.
description: This recipe installs SparkLing 0.1.0 at the immutable product revision recorded in backends/atlas-sparkling/pins-0.1.0.json (a draft until the release is built). The Atlas engine image is built from Enntity/SparkLing by install/build.sh and published to GHCR; LLooM commits no engine source. Setup acquires the selected checkpoint at its pinned revision (primitive-ai/Ling-3.2-air-NVFP4A16 for spark, inclusionAI/Ling-3.2-air for strict), pulls the image by its manifest digest and verifies it, then runs SparkLing's own install/check_files.py with install/checkpoint.json, fetched at the pinned revision, digest-checked and run inside the image with no network, to check every inference file against its pinned size and hash. Nothing is assembled: the engine serves the checkpoint directory as downloaded. Setup remembers the weights it installed with.

provenance.source: SparkLing 0.1.0 (draft): Enntity/SparkLing at the revision pins-0.1.0.json will record, engine Enntity/atlas at the commit it will record (AGPL-3.0-only, recorded in the image's /opt/atlas/source-manifest.json). Image ghcr.io/enntity/atlas-sparkling:<first 12 characters of the install/ tree>, addressed by its GHCR manifest digest. Profiles default.json (0.80 GPU memory utilization, 8 sequences, 262144 tokens), saver.json (0.70, 1, 8192) and max.json (0.88, 16, 262144), all with BF16 KV and prefix caching. Checkpoints primitive-ai/Ling-3.2-air-NVFP4A16 revision 3a78e58506316b5b9b7d06037910c3f4abdd291f (MIT) and inclusionAI/Ling-3.2-air revision ff099487f6f57165e6fa9386ad61fddfafc78b76 (MIT), each checked against SparkLing's install/checkpoint.json.

hardware.testedMachine: One DGX Spark with 128 GB unified memory
notes: SparkLing on one GB10, 2026-11-23 (SparkLing README, development build): at 40K context with drafting off, the Spark checkpoint decoded single-stream prose at 43.70 tok/s (vLLM 21.60 on the same Spark and checkpoint) and four prose clients at 83.78 tok/s aggregate; at eight clients vLLM served more. Those runs used the rigmark-40k profile, not this recipe's modes; the 0.1.0 release measurement is not in yet.

Spark mode drafts with the checkpoint's own one-token MTP predictor (SPARKLING_DRAFTER=mtp) for one live request; from two requests the engine decodes plainly. Atlas verifies each draft against the target.
Ling-3.2-air uses its 262,144-token window in the default and max modes; the KV pool is shared across requests. At 256K, Spark mode reads some upper-layer expert weights from the model files.

Draft: SparkLing 0.1.0 is not released. backends/atlas-sparkling/pins-0.1.0.json is a draft whose SparkLing revision, engine commit, image digest and tool digests are placeholders, so setup stops at verify-atlas-pins until the release fills them in. The container image below is the same placeholder. Video input assumes the release ships SparkLing's video profiles (ffmpeg decoding enabled); confirm on the release image before this recipe is final.

Profiles (SparkLing install/profiles, all BF16 KV, 2,048-token prefill chunks or 8,192 with NVFP4 prefill, prefix caching): default 8 requests at 0.80 GPU memory utilization, saver 1 request of 8,192 tokens at 0.70, max 16 requests at 0.88. Requests the KV pool cannot hold yet wait rather than fail. Strict shares one KV pool between requests (ATLAS_KV_MAX_BLOCKS in each profile) and pages cold experts from the checkpoint on disk, so expect it to be much slower than Spark.

Peak host memory was not measured per mode. LLooM reserves an estimate: saver 92 GB, default 104 GB, max 114 GB. The container is capped at 114 GiB because a GB10 that runs out of shared memory hangs instead of killing a process. In the default and max modes little else should use this Spark's GPU memory.

The engine serves 127.0.0.1:8897 (fixed by the image) with host networking, so only one SparkLing model runs at a time; its memory reservation keeps LLooM from starting the other beside it. Text, image and video input: OpenAI image_url parts and video_url parts (animated GIF decoded in-process, MP4 and WebM through the image's ffmpeg).
Licenses: the Atlas engine and SparkLing's install tools run from the image and are AGPL-3.0-only (not included in LLooM). inclusionAI/Ling-3.2-air and primitive-ai/Ling-3.2-air-NVFP4A16 are MIT.

modes.summary: Profile saver: 1 request at 8192 tokens, 0.70 GPU memory utilization, 92 GB reserved (an estimate); leaves room for sidecars.
Profile default: 8 requests at 262144 tokens, 0.80 GPU memory utilization, 104 GB reserved (an estimate).
Profile max: 16 requests at 262144 tokens, 0.88 GPU memory utilization, 114 GB reserved (an estimate).
